title: LIBS 7102 · Lecture 2
subtitle: Conventional morality: conflicts of interest, Piaget and Kohlberg's six stages with stage 4.5, why convention is not the final level, and Singer's "All animals are equal"
description: Lecture 2 of LIBS 7102: the ten conflicts of interest and conventional morality at work; Piaget's two stages; Heinz and Kohlberg's six stages plus 4.5, each with the slide's wording and how it can go wrong; why stage 4 can be a problem and why stage 6 exists beyond democracy; Singer's "All animals are equal": equality as a moral ideal, equal consideration of interests, "Can they suffer?", speciesism and the reply to Frankena. Practice answers K1 to K4 and a 16-item mock quiz.
intro:
:::exam Midterm facts
**Midterm: Wednesday Oct 28, in class.** Closed book, two hours, on paper, 20 % of the course. You write four or five two-paragraph answers, choosing from about six (for example, answer 4 of 6). Questions cover lectures 1 to 5 and are taken from the practice list (rare) or very similar to it (typical), often paired with a computing case or asking you to argue a side. It feeds the four Kohlberg practice questions (K1 to K4).
:::

steps.note: write the six stages plus 4.5 from memory, then answer K1 and K2
answer K3 and K4 in two paragraphs each
say why equal consideration is not equal treatment

lessons.title: Conventional morality is doing what your co-workers and your boss would do
Kohlberg's six stages run from fear of punishment to universal principles
Convention can be flawed or only accidentally right, so the levels go past it
Singer: equality means equal consideration of interests, and the test is suffering
